title: Invocation Attribution Rundown & Pricing Modules (console prototype)
creator: Ava Morrison
description:
Problem: Customers want a compact, exportable view in Redwood Console that lets engineers and finance teams understand per-invocation token cost breakdowns, attribute spend to routes/models/prompts, and preview pricing changes without leaving the dashboard. Current cost views are high-level; teams struggle to drill into anomalous spikes and to generate CSVs suitable for chargeback.

Goal: Deliver a token-level Attribution Rundown component + Pricing Modules that fits into the Console Route & Cost pages. Primary outcomes: fast triage of cost anomalies, clear cost attribution to route/model/prompt shape, and an interactive pricing preview (ratebook toggles + what-if slider for batching/quantization) that updates cost forecasts in real time. Must support export (CSV/Parquet) and be accessible/performance-minded for large datasets.
user_stories: As an SRE, I can open a per-route Invocation Attribution panel and see token-level cost slices (prompt vs. completion, system vs. user) so I can understand where latency and spend originate.
As a Finance PM, I can apply a ratebook override and export a filtered CSV of attribution rows for chargeback to downstream accounting.
As an engineer, I can toggle a ‘simulate batch/quantize’ slider to preview how unit costs would change under a Dedicated profile and compare delta to current hosted pricing.
acceptance_criteria: Rundown component renders aggregated rows grouped by route, model, and prompt template with per-row token counts and cost; totals match server-side aggregation (within 0.5%).
Export button downloads full filtered dataset as CSV and Parquet (schema documented in spec).

Pricing Module allows ratebook override and a what-if slider; cost forecast updates within 500ms for datasets <= 2k rows, and shows a progressive spinner for larger data sets with server-side pagination in place.
All interactive controls are keyboard navigable and pass color-contrast and ARIA label checks documented in the accessibility checklist.
Design handoff includes Figma tokens, annotated CSS tokens (spacing/color/typography), and labelled assets; engineering has a short checklist for virtualization and memoization to avoid 60fps jank.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: client-side full-table rendering for rich interactions vs. server-side aggregation for scale. We will implement server-driven aggregation with a virtualized row list to support drilldowns to individual invocations. The Pricing Module will initially support the two most common ratebooks (hosted, dedicated) and provide an API hook for custom enterprise ratebooks in a later sprint. To preserve customer privacy, raw prompt text will be redacted by default and requires a permission flag to unredact in workspace settings.
implementation_guidance: Engineering: use existing /costs/attribution endpoint (ENG-72011) and add query params for ratebook_override and simulation_flags. UI should use windowed list (react-window) and batch updates via PATCH subscription to reduce re-rendering. For export, call the export job endpoint and stream via signed URL. Provide an initial row schema: [timestamp, route, model, prompt_template_id (redacted), tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, unit_cost_usd, cost_usd, ratebook_id].
accessibility_considerations: 1) All action buttons (Export, Simulate, Ratebook) have aria-labels and focus states. 2) Table supports row selection via keyboard and exposes aria-rowcount. 3) Redaction toggle has clear label and state; audit log records who unredacted. 4) High-contrast theme adjustments available as an on-panel toggle.
performance_constraints: Must support up to 100k attribution rows over time; UI should fetch aggregated pages of 200 rows by default and allow ‘full export’. Cost simulation runs on the server; UI caches last simulation per session to avoid repeated compute. When applying a what-if slider, UI performs optimistic delta math for immediate feedback and reconciles with server result when available.
rollout_plan: 1) Alpha: internal-only behind feature flag for Redwood SREs & finance team (2 weeks) -> collect feedback on missing columns and export schema. 2) Beta: opt-in for customers with > $5k monthly spend; add telemetry to capture export usage and simulation frequency. 3) GA: exposed to all workspaces with release notes and short doc in Console Help centre.
metrics: Adoption: % of routes using Attribution Rundown after 30 days, Export usage per workspace, Simulation usage per workspace, Reduction in support tickets for unknown spikes (target -30%).
